title: The Wild Boar and the Fox
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Wild Boar was engaged in whetting his tusks upon the trunk of a tree in the forest when a Fox came by and, seeing what he was at, said to him, "Why are you doing that, pray? The huntsmen are not out to-day, and there are no other dangers at hand that I can see." "True, my friend," replied the Boar, "but the instant my life is in danger I shall need to use my tusks. There'll be no time to sharpen them then."

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what is the Wild Boar doing at the start?
options: Digging for roots beneath the tree
Resting in the shade of the forest
Whetting his tusks upon the trunk of a tree
Chasing a smaller animal through the trees

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Fox point out about the day?
options: That the huntsmen are not out and no other dangers are at hand
That a storm is approaching from the north
That other boars have already been seen sharpening their tusks
That the forest is unusually quiet today

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Boar say he will need his tusks for?
options: Digging up food during the winter
Marking his territory in the forest
Defending his young from other boars
The instant his life is in danger

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Boar say there will be no time for once danger arrives?
options: To find a place to hide
To sharpen his tusks
To call for help from other boars
To finish whetting the tree

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does the Boar address the Fox in his reply?
options: "Stranger"
"Neighbor"
"My friend"
"Sir Fox"

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Boar sharpen his tusks even though no danger is currently present?
options: He prepares in advance, knowing there will be no time once danger actually arrives
He enjoys the activity regardless of any practical use
He is trying to impress the Fox with his strength
He misunderstood the Fox's warning about huntsmen

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Fox's question reveal about his own way of thinking?
options: He believes the Boar is wasting time on an impossible task
He is trying to warn the Boar of danger he has already seen
He wants to learn how to sharpen his own teeth
He only sees the value of an action if the danger is immediate and visible

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "whetting" mean in "whetting his tusks"?
options: Cleaning
Sharpening
Measuring
Hiding

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "at hand" mean in "no other dangers at hand"?
options: Forgotten or ignored
Expected soon
Nearby or present
Discussed openly

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: It is wise to prepare for danger before it actually arrives
Wild boars are naturally more cautious than foxes
Sharpening tusks is only useful during a hunt
Danger always comes with plenty of warning

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who comes upon the Boar while he is sharpening his tusks?
options: A group of huntsmen
Another Boar
A passing deer
A Fox

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Fox ask the Boar?
options: Where he plans to travel next
Why he is sharpening his tusks
How old his tusks are
Whether he has seen any huntsmen

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what single word does the Boar use to agree with the Fox's observation?
options: "Yes"
"Indeed"
"True"
"Perhaps"

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why doesn't the Boar wait until danger actually appears before sharpening his tusks?
options: He knows that sharpening takes time he would not have in a real emergency
He believes sharpening only works if done well in advance of any threat
He is simply bored and looking for something to do
He wants to frighten the Fox into leaving him alone

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what assumption does the Fox make that the Boar's answer corrects?
options: That tusks are not actually useful for self-defense
That huntsmen never hunt boars in this forest
That the Boar is not strong enough to need tusks at all
That preparation is only worthwhile when a threat is already visible

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "the instant" mean in "the instant my life is in danger"?
options: Sometime later
The very moment
Once a year
Only rarely

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Fox teaches a Boar how to sharpen his tusks properly
A Boar and a Fox flee together from approaching huntsmen
A Boar explains to a puzzled Fox why he prepares for danger before it arrives
A Fox convinces the Boar to stop sharpening his tusks
